payload.text:
You are a world-class luxury hotel interior designer, architectural visualization expert,
and hospitality brand consultant with 20+ years of experience.

You specialize EXCLUSIVELY in 4-star and 5-star hotel CORRIDOR design.
You understand hotel circulation psychology, guest comfort, luxury perception,
lighting standards, material realism, and brand consistency.

Your work is realistic, buildable, and presentation-ready for hotel owners,
investors, and architects.
--------------------------------------------------------------------

INPUT STRUCTURE YOU WILL RECEIVE:

1) BRAND REFERENCE IMAGES
These images represent the official interior design identity of
Golden Carthage Hotel, located in Gammarth, Tunis.

2) TARGET CORRIDOR IMAGE
This is a real photograph of a hotel corridor that needs interior redesign.

3) OPTIONAL USER EDIT PROMPT
A short instruction such as:
“Make it warmer”
“More luxurious”
“More Arabic influence”
“More modern”
“Darker lighting”
“More minimalist”
--------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 1 — BRAND DNA ANALYSIS (INTERNAL)
Analyze the brand reference images and extract:
- Color palette
- Material language
- Lighting mood
- Luxury level
- Cultural influences (Mediterranean / North African / Contemporary)
- Emotional atmosphere
- Brand personality

This brand DNA MUST guide all designs.

--------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 2 — ARCHITECTURAL RESPECT (MANDATORY)
You MUST NOT change:
- Corridor dimensions
- Door locations
- Ceiling height
- Structural walls
- Perspective or camera angle

You MAY change ONLY:
- Wall finishes and textures
- Carpets or flooring
- Ceiling details and lighting
- Decorative wall elements
- Color palettes
- Materials and finishes
- Lighting temperature and ambiance

All results must be realistic and suitable for real hotel construction.

--------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 3 — DESIGN TASK
Redesign the target corridor using the Golden Carthage brand identity.

Generate EXACTLY 5 DISTINCT interior design concepts for the SAME corridor.
Each concept must be:
- Luxury hotel standard
- Photorealistic
- Elegant and refined
- Calm and welcoming
- Suitable for a premium hospitality environment

--------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 4 — STYLE DIRECTIONS (GENERATE ALL 5)

1) MODERN MEDITERRANEAN LUXURY
- Warm neutral tones
- Natural stone or travertine textures
- Soft indirect lighting
- Relaxed yet elegant atmosphere

2) CONTEMPORARY TUNISIAN ELEGANCE
- Subtle North African motifs
- Refined geometric patterns
- Brass or gold accents
- Cultural luxury without exaggeration

3) HIGH-END MINIMAL MODERN
- Clean architectural lines
- Premium materials
- Minimal decoration
- Strong but soft lighting design

4) BOUTIQUE HOTEL ARTISTIC STYLE
- Textured or sculpted walls
- Statement lighting
- Artistic carpet or wall details
- Unique yet elegant personality

5) TIMELESS CLASSIC LUXURY
- Rich and noble materials
- Elegant wall panels or moldings
- Warm classic lighting
- Prestigious, calm atmosphere

--------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 5 — USER EDIT PROMPT (IF PROVIDED)
If a user edit prompt is provided, apply it intelligently
to ALL 5 designs while preserving:
- Luxury quality
- Brand identity
- Architectural realism

Do NOT exaggerate or distort the design.

--------------------------------------------------------------------

STEP 6 — OUTPUT REQUIREMENTS (CRITICAL)
- Output EXACTLY 5 photorealistic images
- Keep the SAME camera angle as the original corridor
- Each image must represent ONE of the 5 styles
- No text, labels, or watermarks inside images
- Ultra-realistic lighting, materials, and shadows
- Hotel brochure / investor presentation quality

Your final output must look like it was designed by a top international
hospitality interior design studio.

**Visualizing the Design**

I'm now picturing the core functionality: a React app for visualizing corridor redesigns. The "Golden Carthage Hotel" brand identity is central to this design tool. I see this app providing an interface to explore and iterate on different design options.


**Defining Core Features**

I've been solidifying the core features. Input will consist of brand reference images, a target corridor image, and an optional text prompt. The Gemini API will process this to create five distinct corridor redesign concepts. The output will display these images, likely offering download options. We're prioritizing integration of the detailed system instructions into the Gemini prompt for optimal results.


**Assessing Gemini Capabilities**

I'm now zeroing in on Gemini-3-pro-image-preview. This multimodal model is perfect for the task, taking multiple images and text for nuanced output. I've realized its strengths in handling architectural constraints, so I'm structuring the prompt as an image-based transformation. The application skeleton is taking shape, with metadata, the React entry, and the HTML entry point.


**Structuring the UI Components**

I'm organizing the UI components. `App.tsx` will manage the main layout and state. The brand will be featured in `Header.tsx`, with image uploads handled by `UploadSection.tsx`. `PromptInput.tsx` will collect user instructions, and `Gallery.tsx` will present the image results. I'll use `LoadingOverlay.tsx` for feedback during generation. Finally, `geminiService.ts` will manage the Gemini API interactions.


**Prioritizing API Implementation**

I've realized a critical step for `gemini-3-pro-image-preview`: the mandatory API key selection. I have to integrate `window.aistudio.openSelectKey()`.

I'm now focusing on designing the user interface. I'm imagining a luxury aesthetic with gold, black, white, cream, and deep blue, incorporating serif headings and sans-serif elements. A vertical flow—uploads, configuration, generation, then gallery—seems like the ideal layout. Finally, I need to decide on the Gemini API calls: Either five separate parallel calls, or a single call requesting five variations. The prompt will be constructed to integrate user provided system instructions, which I'll send to the model with the reference images.


**Refining Generation Strategy**

I'm now zeroing in on the image generation strategy. The goal is to get five distinct results, which requires careful prompt engineering. I'll construct a prompt that leverages the style variations. Instead of making five separate calls for each design, I'll iterate through the five styles I've defined, sending each specific prompt to Gemini. This ensures the output reflects the intended distinct styles, and hopefully ensures five images total.


**Crafting Precise Prompts**

I'm now revising the prompting strategy for Gemini. For each of the five styles, I'll send the target corridor image and brand reference images. The text prompt will be: "Redesign this corridor... Style: [Specific Style]... [User Edit Prompt]... Maintain perspective." I am focusing on the exact wording for clarity and consistency with the image model.


**Formulating API Integration**

I'm now integrating the user's system prompt and my style definitions into the API calls. I'm focusing on the `GeminiService` function `generateDesigns`, which will manage the requests, and should either return a promise or a stream of results. Sequential API calls are favored for user feedback and potential rate limit management. I'm leaning toward a high-end, clean architectural look for the UI, considering a light or dark mode. No camera or mic permissions needed, just file uploads. I'm ready to start coding.


**Managing API Requests**

I'm now prioritizing the API call sequencing. I've decided to manage API requests sequentially using either a queue system or a `for...of` loop with `await` to process them. This ensures a smoother UI experience. After considering the "High-Quality Image Generation" request, I remain committed to `gemini-3-pro-image-preview`. Also, I've confirmed that I must use `await window.aistudio.hasSelectedApiKey()`

The prompt will be: Text: [Role Definition] ... [Task Description] ... [Style Description] ... [User Prompt] Images: [Target Image] ... [Brand Images].


**Organizing Image Data**

I'm making progress clarifying the image inputs. I'll explicitly specify in the prompt which image is the target corridor and which are style guides. The array of image parts sent to the model will reflect this order, ensuring the "Target" image is first. Dependencies for UI components and transitions are selected: `lucide-react`, and standard Tailwind transitions are preferred for now. The file layout has been mapped out, including a file to handle key selection with `window.aistudio`, and to handle the image inputs, all the way to `App.tsx`.


**Formulating the Final Prompt**

I'm now integrating the user's system instructions into the prompt. The final structure takes shape: I'll iterate through each defined style, crafting a detailed prompt including role definition, input context, task description (specifying style and constraints), and the user's edit, all while prioritizing a single, photorealistic output. I'm focusing on managing multiple images: `gemini-3-pro-image-preview` is the best, but I should limit brand image uploads to prevent exceeding the payload size. It's time to build.
